Hannah — I ran the Stagehand CSV through our capacity model and put a short summary below. High-level recommendation: provision for sustained 95th traffic + 1.4x safety on peak patterns, with a short warm-up canary before full swap.

Summary (proposed):
- GPU type: 8x A100s (40GB, fp16 optimized) per node; prefer q4_0 quantization path for the current model family.
- Node count (initial): 6 nodes (48 GPUs total) — estimated sustained throughput capacity ~260k token RPM with batching + KV cache enabled.
- Safety multiplier: 1.4x applied to 99th burst forecast = plan for transient headroom to ~504k token RPM.
- Cache config: enable prefix/KV caching on 70% of requests (Stagehand can mark stable prompt families) — reduces per-token compute by ~22% in our sim.
- Validation cadence:
  - Day 0 (precut): configuration validation + smoke test (2h)
  - Day 1: 24h soak with mirrored traffic at 25–50% (read-only routing)
  - Day 3: 6h stress run at 110% of observed 99th (billing-sandboxed)
  - Day 4: Post-stress observability review and sign-off
- Cutover timeline (two-week window suggestion):
  - Week 1: Stand up dedicated fleet, baseline tests, mirrored soak (non-traffic impacting)
  - Week 2, Day 1: Canary switch (5% traffic -> monitor 6h)
  - Week 2, Day 2: Ramp to 25% (monitor 12h)
  - Week 2, Day 3: Ramp to 60% (monitor 12h)
  - Week 2, Day 4: Full swap (final 2h blackout window planned)
  - Rollback: immediate revert to hosted route within 30 minutes for any critical SLA violation; full fallback pattern scripted.

Risks & mitigations:
- Tail latency spikes: mitigate via transient capacity autoscale policy + adjusted batching windows.
- Cache warmup: pre-populate KV for top 50 prompt families during soak.
- Double-run cost: recommend a staged ramp (canary->partial->full) to minimize overlap billing.

Attachments: I exported the run numbers into stagehand_capacity_model_review.csv (I'll drop in the HubSpot link).

I'll join the customer runbook review if you want me on the call.
